To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the type and amount (flux) of sediment produced in the euphotical zone (bioclastic, grain- or framework-producing biota) and its dispersal are the main controlling factors of the stratal patterns and architecture of carbonate platforms; (2) in carbonate platforms, base level for the accumulation of sediment (accommodation) is not a fixed factor; it is controlled by the sediment flux and the processes of sediment dispersal.

in carbonates the amount of accommodation space available for sediment to accumulate depends on the amount of sediment being deposited and the processes controlling sedimentation and dispersal, as well as on the type of biota producing the sediment.

in carbonate settings the accommodation space available for sediment to accumulate depends on the type of sediment being deposited and the processes controlling its dispersal and that this space is not independent from the amount of sediment produced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of accommodation by biological processes and the resulting facies architecture in carbonates.
the ecological control on the sedimentary response to sea-level changes.
the interdependence between accommodation and sediment flux, and how it affects the internal architecture of depositional sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the accommodation space is controlled by sediment flux, and the sediment flux is controlled by ecological factors.
the evolution of the Balearics carbonate platform was the result of a change in ecological control of sedimentary processes and accommodation.
, in carbonate systems, accommodation is controlled by the type and amount and locus of the sediment produced and by the biological system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accommodation space available to the carbonate system is not independent of the carbonate system, as it is in siliciclastics.

the stratal pattern, facies architecture and heterogeneity distribution of the Upper Miocene carbonate platform in the Balearic Basin were the result of a combination of factors, among them the ecological control of the sedimentary processes and of accommodation.

, in carbonate systems, the accommodation for sediment accumulation is not independent of the sediment being produced and that the base level for sediment dispersal depends on both the amount and type (loose or framework) of the carbonate factory.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the accommodation space for sediment accumulation in carbonates is not independent from the type and amount, but also from the production loci of the carbonate factory, and from the type of sediment dispersal.
the type of carbonate factory and the processes controlling its development are crucial to understand the internal facies architecture of the carbonate platform.
, in carbonates, accommodation is a dynamic parameter that depends on sediment production, sediment dispersal, and base level.
